Specify the between-response graph layer

Source: R/between_graph.R
mc_between_graph.Rd

Builds the specification object that controls how the between-response covariance \(\Sigma_b\) of the Pearson residuals is parametrized in mcglm_graph. Two layers are available.

  • "ggm", the Gaussian graphical model (GGM): the precision matrix is linear in the parameters, \(K_b = \Sigma_b^{-1} = \sum_d \eta_d Z_d\), with one diagonal parameter per response and one parameter per edge (see mc_precision_bases). A missing edge sets the corresponding precision entry, and hence the partial correlation, to zero.

  • "dag", the directed acyclic graph (DAG) layer, through the modified Cholesky (LDL) factorization \(\Sigma_b = T^{-1} D T^{-\top}\), with \(T = I - \Gamma\) unit lower triangular in the given ordering, \(\Gamma\) holding the structural coefficients \(\gamma_{ji}\) on the edges, and \(D = \mathrm{diag}(\delta_1, \dots, \delta_R)\) the innovation variances. Each response is regressed on its parents.

Usage

mc_between_graph(type = c("ggm", "dag"), edges = NULL, ordering = NULL)

Arguments

type

character, the layer: "ggm" for the Gaussian graphical model (precision-based) or "dag" for the directed acyclic graph (modified Cholesky).

edges

optional integer matrix with columns \((i, j)\) giving the edges as response positions; NULL means the complete graph. A matrix with no rows is the empty graph. The edges are stored in canonical form, each pair with \(i < j\) and the rows in lexicographic order, which is the order of the edge parameters, so the order in which they are supplied does not matter. In the DAG layer an edge is an adjacency and its direction is set by ordering.

ordering

optional integer permutation of 1:R defining the ordering of the DAG layer: an edge points from the response that comes first in ordering to the one that comes later. The default is the natural order. It has no meaning for type = "ggm", whose precision support is unordered, and supplying it there is an error rather than a silently ignored argument.

Value

An object of class "mcg_graph_spec": a list with components type, edges (canonical edge matrix or NULL) and ordering (integer vector or NULL).

References

Dempster, A. P. (1972). Covariance selection. Biometrics, 28(1), 157-175. doi:10.2307/2528966

Lauritzen, S. L. (1996). Graphical Models. Oxford University Press.

Pourahmadi, M. (1999). Joint mean-covariance models with applications to longitudinal data: unconstrained parameterisation. Biometrika, 86(3), 677-690. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.3.677

See also

mcglm_graph, mc_build_sigma_between_graph

Examples

mc_between_graph("ggm")
#> $type
#> [1] "ggm"
#> 
#> $edges
#> NULL
#> 
#> $ordering
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcg_graph_spec"
mc_between_graph("dag", edges = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)))
#> $type
#> [1] "dag"
#> 
#> $edges
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
#> [2,]    2    3
#> 
#> $ordering
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "mcg_graph_spec"
